verdict: Chicken nuggets are the better pick. Fewer calories and much more protein, so they're more filling.
why: 6 nuggets are an estimated 280 kcal, medium fries an estimated 340 kcal. You save around 60 kcal.
Nuggets have 14 g protein, fries only 4 g. A big difference for feeling full.
Fat is about the same: 17 g vs 16 g. Both are fried.
Fries are very easy to eat without noticing, one after another, and you get hungry again quickly.
when_a: Fries are okay when you share one box with your kids or friends, or take a small size as a side.
when_b: Nuggets are okay as a snack or a simple side dish. 6 pieces is enough, no need for 9 or 20.
tip: Dip lightly in chilli or tomato sauce. Mayo and cheese sauce can add calories without you noticing.

faq.q: Nuggets are processed food, is that okay?
faq.a: They can fit once in a while. For everyday meals, grilled chicken or normal home-cooked chicken is more filling. But if these two are your only choices, nuggets help more.

faq.q: I really love fries. Do I have to stop completely?
faq.a: No need. Take a small size, eat slowly, and pair it with a protein source. Controlling how often matters more than banning it.
